title: Pay Per Call Affiliate Payouts: How to Automate Them
h1: Pay per call affiliate payouts: how to automate them
description: Pay per call affiliate payouts without spreadsheets: set rates per affiliate, define payable calls and share statements. See the steps.
faq: How do I pay pay-per-call affiliates automatically?

Give each affiliate their own tracking numbers and payout rate, write down what counts as a payable call, and let your software apply those rules to every call and produce a statement from the same record.
What is a payable call in pay per call?

It is a call that meets the agreed rules, such as a minimum duration, a caller in the right location and not a blocked or repeat caller. The buyer and the network should agree this in writing before traffic starts.
How do I avoid payout disputes with affiliates?
Use one call record that both sides can see, attribute each call to a source with its own tracking number, and explain in writing how disputed calls are handled before the first payout.
body:
Pay per call affiliate payouts are easiest to run automatically when three things are fixed in advance: a payout rate for each affiliate, a written rule for which calls are payable, and one call record that both sides can check. If the software applies those rules to every call and produces a statement from the same data, you stop rebuilding spreadsheets at the end of each period, and affiliates stop asking why their number looks different from yours.

Why pay per call affiliate payouts go wrong by hand

Manual payouts usually fail in the same few places. Each affiliate was promised a different rate, and the rate lives in an email thread. The buyer disputes a handful of calls and nobody can say which affiliate sent them. The affiliate keeps their own count, the network keeps another, and the two never quite match. Month-end turns into a reconciliation project.

Automation does not remove disagreements, but it moves them to the start of the relationship, where they are cheap to settle, instead of the end of the month, where they are not.

Step 1: Decide what makes a call payable

Before you can pay anyone automatically, you need a definition a machine can apply. Write down, for each campaign:

  • The minimum call duration that counts.
  • Which countries or states the caller must be in.
  • Whether repeat callers are paid more than once.
  • Which numbers are blocked and never paid.
  • Any hours or daily caps set by the buyer.

These are the same rules that protect your buyer, so setting them once serves both sides. If you are still choosing how to structure them, the guide to pay per call campaign setup walks through the order to do it in.

Step 2: Give every affiliate a rate and their own numbers

Payouts can only be automatic if each call is already tied to the affiliate who sent it. That means every traffic source gets its own tracking number, so a call is attributed the moment it arrives rather than guessed at later. Then set a payout rate per affiliate. Two affiliates on the same offer can have different rates, and a new affiliate can start on a different rate than a proven one. Keep those rates in the system, not in a message history.

Think about the margin too. Your payout to the affiliate should sit below what the buyer pays you, and the gap needs to cover your costs. Decide that before you quote a rate, not after.

Step 3: Let call quality affect who gets paid

Paying for every call, regardless of quality, rewards the wrong behavior. A source that sends many very short calls costs you money if the buyer will not pay for them. Grade your sources, watch the share of short calls, and pause a source that keeps sending them. Doing this by rule rather than by mood makes the conversation with the affiliate much easier, because the evidence is the same record for both of you. For more on this, see how call quality grading works.

Step 4: Give affiliates their own view of the numbers

Most payout arguments are really visibility arguments. If affiliates can log in and see their own calls, durations and earnings, they do not need to email you for a number. A portal for affiliates and one for buyers means each party sees the part that concerns them, and a downloadable statement gives everyone the same document at the end of the period. The money side of the product is covered under payouts and statements.

Step 5: Reconcile against the buyer before you pay out

The safest order is: buyer confirms the calls, you apply any adjustments, then affiliates are paid on the adjusted figures. If a buyer disputes a call, you need to be able to find that exact call, its length and its source. Keep recordings or transcripts where your rules allow it. Your obligations around call recording and consent vary, so check them with your own counsel.

It also helps to be clear with affiliates, in writing, about how disputed calls are handled before the first payout is due. That one paragraph prevents most awkward conversations later.

How this works in Insight Dial

These steps map to features that are already in the platform:

  • Per-affiliate payout rates: set a rate for each affiliate, so every call is credited at the right amount.
  • Call tracking numbers per source: dynamic number insertion and dedicated numbers tie each call to its source.
  • Routing rules: hours, daily caps, state rules, blocked numbers and repeat-caller blocks apply before a call is transferred.
  • Quality grades: Good, Watch and Poor grades, with auto-pause of sources sending too many short calls.
  • Affiliate and buyer portals: each side can see its own records, and statements can be downloaded.
  • Webhooks: signed webhooks with a delivery log and an open API let you pass call data to your own systems.

Pricing is pay as you go, with a per-minute call rate and a monthly price per tracking number from a topped-up balance. Details are on the pricing page.

A simple payout routine

  1. Agree the payable-call definition with the buyer.
  2. Set each affiliate's rate and give them dedicated tracking numbers.
  3. Test-call every number before live traffic.
  4. Check quality grades weekly, not only at period end.
  5. Share statements, settle disputes from the call record, then pay.

If your vertical is regulated or has strict buyer rules, such as insurance or legal, tighten the payable-call definition first and keep a clear record of each decision.
